newsitem.title: ESTONIA: EU PRAISES ECONOMY, STRESSES RUSSIAN MINORITY.
newsitem.headline: EU PRAISES ECONOMY, STRESSES RUSSIAN MINORITY.

text.p: The European Commission on Wednesday said that Estonia had a functioning market economy but needed to do more to naturalise its large Russian minority.
The Commission made the conclusion as it recommended talks begin with Estonia on EU entry along with four other eastern European nations: Poland, Slovenia, Hungary and the Czechs.

"Estonia can be regarded as a functioning market economy and it should be able to make the progress necessary to cope with the competitive pressure and market forces within the Union in the medium term," the Commission said.
It said Estonia was a democracy with stable institutions.
"But measures need to be taken to accelerate the naturalisation of Russian-speaking non-citizens, to enable them to become better integrated into Estonian society," it added.
The report also said that Estonia had made steps to implement a single market.
"With further effort it should be able to participate fully in the single market in the medium term," it added.
It said that massive investment was needed in the field of the environment and to strengthen its administrative structure.
The report praised the bank sector as healthy and expanding.
But it said the country's export base was narrow and that the need to finance a rising trade and current account deficit was a matter of concern.
The Commission is to report no later than the end of next year on the progress Estonia has achieved to meet the recommendations of the conclusion.
